tweets: Price oracle manipulation exploits vulnerabilities in price feeds to alter contract logic, potentially causing unauthorized actions or fund loss.
This risk stems from relying on a single data source that can be manipulated by malicious actors.
A primary defense is aggregating multiple decentralized oracle sources rather than trusting one feed.
When using aggregated data, reject outliers and anomalous deviations to prevent skewed pricing decisions.
Implement Time-Weighted Average Prices (TWAP) over sufficient windows to resist short-lived price manipulations.
Design your system to avoid basing core prices on illiquid pools, as these are more susceptible to manipulation.
Include fail-safe behavior that halts sensitive operations like borrowing or liquidations when data is suspicious or unavailable.
Use circuit breakers and rate limiting on parameter changes to prevent rapid exploitation of oracle feeds.
